clue.text: Hide as Conservative involved in business purchase

indicators.note: the abbreviation is caught up within the other word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a takeover is one company buying another

explanation.surface: A Tory hides away while caught up in a corporate buyout.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter from danger or view is to hide, the same sense as the phrase.

clue.text: The heartless Dickensian sycophant letting out quiet chuckle

indicators.note: the middle of the three-letter word is removed
the soft-playing letter is released from the name

parts.note: Uriah Heep, the fawning clerk in David Copperfield
P for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A heartless Dickensian toady gives a little quiet chuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitative word for a giggle or snigger, so a small chuckle.

clue.text: Most considerate type taking time in Panama for example

parts.note: kind means type or sort
EST, Eastern Standard Time, kept in Panama

explanation.surface: The most thoughtful sort takes his time in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' tempts you towards a hat; Panama keeps Eastern Standard Time all year.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of kind, showing the greatest thought for others.

clue.text: Provide food and drink support — grub you may not want to eat!

parts.note: to cater is to supply meals
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: Supplying food and drink, but here is grub nobody would eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, the catering theme; it is the larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva of a butterfly or moth, a grub in the entomological sense rather than food.

clue.text: Very English resort, a major tourist attraction

parts.note: Nice, the resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A very English seaside resort that draws crowds of tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon city of canals attracts millions of visitors every year.

clue.text: Group of engineers passes on repairs

parts.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army
dies, as in passes away

explanation.surface: A unit of engineers passes on repair work.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy is to put right, so the verb form means fixes or repairs.

clue.text: Stern-faced little pet in toddler's book?

parts.note: po-faced means stern and humourless; the crossword shortens it to its first part
a pup is a young dog, a small pet

explanation.surface: A stern-looking puppy appears in a picture book for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: PO comes from 'po-faced', British slang for solemn or disapproving; the clue trims it to PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Books with cardboard figures that spring up when a page opens are made chiefly for very young children.

clue.text: Dad getting cross? Let's have peace!

parts.note: pa, a familiar word for father
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Dad is getting cross, so let's call a truce!
explanation.walkthrough: British schoolchildren call out this word to ask for a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for peace, used as a schoolyard interjection calling a truce.

clue.text: Quiet tenant may be someone to whom gratitude is due

definitions.text: someone to whom gratitude is due

parts.note: P for piano, quietly in music
a leaser takes a property on lease

explanation.surface: A quiet tenant may deserve thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives pleasure or satisfaction earns thanks, as in a crowd-pleaser.

clue.text: Friend is given help, not one to be fenced in

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out of the word for helped

parts.note: aided means assisted
I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A friend gets help, but not someone to be fenced in.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes, so something enclosed by one is fenced in.

clue.text: Devon town house that's not fashionable facing west

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means right to left, so the phrase is turned round

parts.note: not in, i.e. out of fashion

explanation.surface: A Devon house that is out of fashion faces west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing west' turns NOT IN round to NITON. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This lace-making market town lies in east Devon, an English county.

clue.text: Rightly following the greatest physicist

indicators.note: the word for rightly comes after the word for the greatest

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the greatest amount
well means rightly or properly, as in 'you did well'

explanation.surface: Rightly coming after the greatest physicist of all.
explanation.definitionFit: James Clerk Maxwell was the Scottish scientist who unified electricity and magnetism.

clue.text: Lady first appearing when it gets dark

definitions.meaning: the first woman in Genesis, wife of Adam
the evening, the time of nightfall

explanation.surface: A lady makes her first appearance once darkness falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblically the first woman; poetically the evening, the close of day when light fades.

clue.text: Verdict is doubly bad for habitual criminals

indicators.note: a bad version of the letters is a corrupted, rearranged one
the little word is to be used two times over

explanation.surface: A verdict that is doubly bad for repeat offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives ISIS; 'bad' shuffles VERDICT with ISIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeat offenders who keep relapsing into crime are the habitual criminals the courts see again and again.

clue.text: Aorta's vol. I can change, diameter having been restricted?

definitions.text: Aorta's vol. I can change, diameter having been restricted?

indicators.note: the measurement letter is confined within the rearranged letters
the letters are able to alter their order

explanation.surface: A medical note on how the aorta's volume can change once its width is constricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can change' gives the anagram VASOILATOR, and 'having been restricted' confines D within it; the whole clue doubles as a description of the drug's effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that widens blood vessels, changing the volume of blood an artery carries whose width was narrowed.

clue.text: Corrupt place needing purge

parts.note: to put something is to place it
to rid is to clear out, to purge

explanation.surface: A corrupt place in need of a purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten and decaying, used figuratively for morally corrupt or depraved.

clue.text: Expectations to have various coppers on street after upset

indicators.note: the letters are taken in a varied, new order
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Expect a range of police officers to be on the street after a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges COPPERS to PROSPEC; 'upset' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Future chances or hopes, so what one may look forward to: expectations.

clue.text: Getting guided around, I certainly will be unhurried

indicators.note: the word for guided goes round the other pieces

parts.note: led is the past of lead, to guide
sure, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: Being shown around, I will certainly take my time.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of free time, so relaxed and unhurried in manner.

clue.text: American university not against getting external support

indicators.note: the word for support goes on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a stand is a supporting frame
for, in favour of

explanation.surface: An American university not opposed to outside funding.
explanation.definitionFit: The private Californian institution near Palo Alto is a leading US university.

clue.text: Out-of-date old boys look back, wanting summer in Paris

parts.note: OBs, former pupils of a school

indicators.note: the short word for look is read backwards

parts.note: lo, an old exclamation meaning look
été is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: Old boys reminisce, missing summer in Paris, all out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: No longer in use or fashion, superseded and therefore out-of-date.

clue.text: Move apace, determined to bag record

indicators.note: the word for determined captures the record within it

parts.note: stout, as in stout resistance, resolute
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Hurrying, resolved to grab a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to walk briskly, to move apace.

clue.text: Burdened, with leader gone — it's rotten

indicators.note: the word for burdened loses its opening letter

parts.note: saddled, as in saddled with debt

explanation.surface: Weighed down and leaderless, it has gone rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of an egg that has gone bad and become putrid.

clue.text: Descent with rope possibly taking a long time

parts.note: a line is a rope, for example on a ship
an age, as in 'it took an age'

explanation.surface: Abseiling down with a rope can take ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' and 'rope' paint a climber; the definition means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or line of family descent from forebears.

clue.text: Show moves around, late getting away

indicators.note: the four letters of the word for tardy escape from the longer word

parts.note: circulates, as at a party

explanation.surface: A travelling show keeps moving on, the late ones escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' is removed as written from CIRCULATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling entertainment with acrobats and clowns is a show.

clue.text: Shop's final salesperson managed to call just before dinner?

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for shop is taken

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
ran, as in ran a business
to dial is to telephone

explanation.surface: A shop's last salesperson manages to ring just before dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a drink or the time immediately before a meal, from Latin prandium.

clue.text: Problem, not the first, to make one worry

indicators.note: the word for problem loses its opening letter

parts.note: a snag is a hitch or problem

explanation.surface: A problem that isn't the first to cause worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone persistently, causing them annoyance and anxiety.

clue.text: City has good hospital department for otolaryngology

parts.note: H for hospital, as on road signs
ENT, ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A city with a good hospital that has an ear, nose and throat unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish city in Belgium, famous for its medieval centre.

clue.text: Small private room with nothing near

parts.note: a closet, originally a small private chamber
O, the figure zero

explanation.surface: A small private room with nothing nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal preposition meaning a short distance from, the same as nearby or near.

clue.text: The artist has such a good sense of music

indicators.note: the two words contain, or have, the short word within them

explanation.surface: The artist has a fine feel for music.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with musical ability is said to have this organ for music, a good sense of it.

clue.text: Old person keeping dry in enclosure, simple accommodation

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed within the word for enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals
TT, a teetotaller who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: An old teetotaller kept in a pen has only basic lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A small modest house, often rural, suggesting plain and humble living quarters.

clue.text: Celebrity entertaining one that's fretted

indicators.note: the word for celebrity hosts the other piece within it

parts.note: a star is a famous person
I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A celebrity entertains someone who has been worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' also serves the definition, 'one that's fretted', the fretted instrument: a double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked Indian lute has frets on its fingerboard, so it is fretted.

clue.text: Get confused in store aimlessly trailing after woman

indicators.note: the shuffled letters follow behind the woman's name

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, a woman's name

indicators.note: moving without purpose suggests letters set in a new random order

explanation.surface: Wandering aimlessly round a store behind a woman, one gets confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone lose their bearings, i.e. to get them confused.
